newsitem.title: LIECHTENSTEIN: Liechtenstein's VP Bank results up in first half.
newsitem.headline: Liechtenstein's VP Bank results up in first half.

text.p: Verwaltungs- und Private-Bank AG (VP Bank) reported half-year results above those of the same 1996 period.
It also said managed assets rose above 20 billion Swiss francs ($13.2 billion) for the first time to 20.7 billion.
At the end of 1996, assets under management were at 19.1 billion Swiss francs.
The bank said its net profit for the first half rose 18 percent to 103.3 million Swiss francs. The figure was pre-tax and before some expenses.

Cash flow also rose by 25 percent to 64.3 million Swiss francs in the first half. The figure was derived from net profits, subtracting personnel costs which were up five percent to 24.3 million, as well as business and office costs of 10 million and taxes of 4.7 million, up 35 percent.
VP Bank was optimistic for the second half of the year, adding that it saw no reason, unlike the previous year, for increased provisions or increased write-offs.

Interest earnings, mainly from its money market activities, rose 14 percent to 36.7 million Swiss francs. Net commission earnings rose 29 percent to 38.6 million, reflecting a favourable bourse trend.
Its total assets at the end of the first half 1997 rose six percent to 7.89 billion Swiss francs.
